fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:.bss
fact_reviews.old_value: During common HSD object-system startup, HSD_ListInitAllocData passes the addresses of slist_alloc_data and dlist_alloc_data to HSD_ObjAllocInit with sizeof(HSD_SList) or sizeof(HSD_DList) and four-byte alignment. Initialization clears and registers each descriptor and derives its aligned node stride. Dedicated getters subsequently expose the descriptors; singly linked node allocation and removal consume slist_alloc_data, while common allocator-statistics reporting reads the counters of both descriptors under the labels "slist" and "dlist".
fact_reviews.reason: Current source, independently read allocator/startup code and observed object metadata support the retained claim.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:.bss
fact_reviews.old_value: An 0x58-byte uninitialized-data section containing two consecutive 0x2C-byte HSD_ObjAllocData objects: slist_alloc_data followed by dlist_alloc_data. Each descriptor stores allocation-limit flags, a free-list head, used/free/peak counters, numeric and heap limits, aligned object size, alignment mask, and a link to the next registered allocator descriptor.
fact_reviews.reason: Current source, independently read allocator/startup code and observed object metadata support the retained claim.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:.bss
fact_reviews.old_value: Provides persistent storage for the HSD list subsystem's two fixed-size object-allocation descriptors: one manages HSD_SList nodes and the other manages HSD_DList nodes.
fact_reviews.reason: Current source, independently read allocator/startup code and observed object metadata support the retained claim.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:.bss
fact_reviews.old_value: The descriptors begin as zero-initialized BSS storage. HSD_ListInitAllocData transitions each to a freshly initialized empty-pool state: prior registry occurrences are removed, the descriptor is cleared, unlimited default limits are installed, four-byte alignment produces an alignment mask of 3, the aligned node stride is recorded, and the descriptor is prepended to the allocator registry. Because slist_alloc_data is initialized first and dlist_alloc_data second, dlist_alloc_data is registered immediately ahead of slist_alloc_data. Subsequent singly linked allocations remove nodes from the slist free list and update used/free/peak counts, while removals return nodes to that free list and reverse the used/free transition.
fact_reviews.reason: Current source, independently read allocator/startup code and observed object metadata support the retained claim.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:.sdata
fact_reviews.old_value: When an HSD_ASSERT condition in list.c is false, compiled code passes the source-file string and the applicable condition string from this contribution, together with the fixed source-line value, to __assert. __assert reports the failed condition and forwards the file and line to HSD_Panic, which invokes the configured panic callback when present and ultimately calls OSPanic. Successful precondition checks take the non-failure path.
fact_reviews.reason: Distinguish literal legacy line values from the actual pinned source lines and record the callback-return condition.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:HSD_DListGetAllocData

That object's allocator configuration originates in HSD_ListInitAllocData, which passes its address, sizeof(HSD_DList), and alignment 4 to HSD_ObjAllocInit; callers of this accessor therefore receive direct access to that persistent initialized descriptor.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:HSD_ListInitAllocData
fact_reviews.old_value: The routine has no caller-supplied inputs or return value. It forwards the addresses of slist_alloc_data and dlist_alloc_data with sizeof(HSD_SList), sizeof(HSD_DList), and alignment 4 to HSD_ObjAllocInit. Each call converts those constants into persistent allocator state by clearing the descriptor, installing default limits, storing an alignment mask of 3, rounding the entry stride, and adding the descriptor to the global allocator registry. The descriptors are subsequently exposed by HSD_SListGetAllocData and HSD_DListGetAllocData; the singly linked descriptor is consumed by node allocation and release, and both descriptors are queried by common allocator-statistics reporting.
fact_reviews.reason: Current source, independently read allocator/startup code and observed object metadata support the retained claim.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:HSD_ListInitAllocData
fact_reviews.old_value: Calling the routine transitions both persistent list descriptors to freshly initialized, registered empty-pool states. For each descriptor, HSD_ObjAllocInit removes any existing registry occurrences, clears all pool state, restores unlimited numeric and heap-derived allocation limits, sets four-byte alignment and the aligned node stride, and reinserts the descriptor at the registry head. Because slist_alloc_data is initialized first and dlist_alloc_data second, the completed registry order places dlist_alloc_data immediately ahead of slist_alloc_data.
fact_reviews.reason: Current source, independently read allocator/startup code and observed object metadata support the retained claim.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/list:HSD_SListAlloc

A successful generic allocation removes one entry from that descriptor's free list and updates its used, free, and peak accounting. HSD_SListAlloc then asserts the returned entry is non-null, clears sizeof(HSD_SList) bytes, and returns the node; callers subsequently populate data and next according to the list being built.

fact_reviews.subject: src/sysdolphin/baselib/list.c
fact_reviews.old_value: Initialization configures separate HSD object allocators for HSD_SList and HSD_DList nodes with four-byte allocation alignment. Singly linked construction obtains a zeroed node from the HSD_SList allocator, stores the caller's opaque payload in data, links the node by rewriting next, and returns the resulting head. Removal saves the current node's successor, returns the node to the same allocator, and returns the saved successor; a null removal input returns null.
fact_reviews.reason: Distinguish append anchor returns from replacement list heads.

fact_reviews.subject: src/sysdolphin/baselib/list.c

fact_reviews.subject: src/sysdolphin/baselib/list.c
fact_reviews.old_value: Implements HSD's shared list infrastructure: it owns object-pool allocator descriptors for singly and doubly linked nodes and provides allocator-backed creation, insertion, and removal operations for singly linked lists carrying opaque payload pointers.
fact_reviews.reason: Current source, independently read allocator/startup code and observed object metadata support the retained claim.

fact_reviews.subject: src/sysdolphin/baselib/list.c
fact_reviews.old_value: During common HSD object startup, the unit reinitializes both persistent list-node allocator descriptors. Each descriptor is removed from any prior registry position, cleared to an empty-pool state, configured with unlimited default limits, a four-byte alignment mask, and the aligned node stride, then inserted at the head of the allocator registry. Its singly linked operations enforce non-null allocation and insertion-node guards, create either singleton or spliced list topologies according to anchor nullness, and transition removal of a non-null head to its saved successor while reclaiming the removed node; removing null leaves the list null.
fact_reviews.reason: State literal mutation boundaries and correct the ambiguous alignment-mask wording.
